gui.hotsteel.codex.title: Chronicle of the Molten Age
hotsteel.chronicle.chapter_1.body:
Long before the Molten Age, the old smiths knew only iron. Then, one night, a furnace was stoked hotter than any before it, and when the slag cooled, a bar of grey steel lay waiting in the ash.

That first crude steel was dark and brittle, yet it held an edge iron never could. They quenched it, folded it, and quenched it again, and from their stubborn hands came the first Steel Ingots.

The chronicle keeps but a single line of that night: “The forge burned until dawn — and dawn was steel.”
hotsteel.chronicle.chapter_1.title: The Birth of Steel
hotsteel.chronicle.chapter_2.body:
Steel alone was not enough. The smiths carried their ingots down to the rivers of fire that run beneath the world, and there, where lava flows like water, they learned to quench steel in the blood of the mountain.

An ingot plunged into the flow did not melt — it drank the heat and rose again as Hot Steel, glowing faintly even in the dark. Those who wore it soon found that flame turned aside, as though the metal still remembered where it was born.

From that day the road to the forge was walked barefoot, and fire ceased to be a danger.
hotsteel.chronicle.chapter_2.title: The Molten Path
hotsteel.chronicle.chapter_3.body:
Deeper still, in the burning places, the smiths met things that were not quite alive: wraiths of flame that whispered in the crackle of the coals and drifted through walls of fire. They named them Fire Wraiths.

Within each wraith burned a Molten Core, a knot of heat so pure it never cooled, even in water. The smiths traded, hunted, and sometimes died for them, for they understood at last that these cores were the key to the Molten Age.

“Wreathed in fire,” the chronicle warns, “they speak only to those who listen to the coals.”
hotsteel.chronicle.chapter_3.title: Souls of the Flame
hotsteel.chronicle.chapter_4.body:
The breakthrough came when a smith pressed a Molten Core into a bar of Hot Steel and struck it, again and again, while it glowed white. Metal and core fused, and what remained on the anvil was neither: Molten Steel.

Heavier than any armour they had known, and hotter, yet it never burned its wearer. To don the full harness was to become part of the forge itself — a Molten Body, untouched by flame or lava, with a heart that beat like a bellows.

“Heavier the iron, hotter the heart,” wrote the smith who first wore it.
hotsteel.chronicle.chapter_4.title: A Body of Molten Steel
hotsteel.chronicle.chapter_5.body:
All that remained was the old rite. Upon the Molten Altar, ringed by a platform of Hot Steel, set down a Molten Core and call the sleeper who has waited since the first furnace was lit: the Ancient Forgeborn.

It has guarded the fire through ages, and it does not yield its treasure lightly. Strike it down, and its heart — the Forge Heart — is yours: a still-burning ember that grants the blessing of the forge.

With the Lord of the Forge fallen, the Molten Age begins.
